items.title: Israel army chief vows to demilitarise Gaza despite ceasefire
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's army chief on Tuesday vowed to push on with demilitarising Gaza and disarming Hamas, despite efforts by the United States to advance the ceasefire in the Palestinian territory. "In Gaza, we are not giving up on the overarching objective – demilitarising the Gaza Strip and disarming Hamas, using all necessary means," Zamir said, according to a military statement. The Israeli military has said that it will keep pursuing alleged perpetrators of Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack.

items.title: Brazil fines TikTok $30 mn in 'powerful signal' over child safety
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazil's data protection agency on Tuesday fined TikTok nearly $30 million for failing to implement child safety measures in what it said was a "powerful signal" to social media companies. Fabricio Lopes, an enforcement director with the ANPD data protection agency, told a press conference that TikTok "was not taking the necessary measures to prevent adolescents from accessing the platform and from having the data of these children and adolescents processed." TikTok agreed last week to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform collected children's personal data without parental permission.

items.title: Scam prevention must evolve as syndicates exploit psychology, AI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to rethink its approach to fighting investment scams as syndicates increasingly rely on sophisticated psychological manipulation rather than simple deception. Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said the sharp rise in cases and losses showed conventional awareness campaigns were no longer sufficient. Sundramoorthy said this amounted to social engineering, where criminals manipulated victims' decision-making rather than merely deceiving them about an investment product.

items.title: 'US set to revoke visas of up to 200,000 foreigners'
items.summary: PRESIDENT Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press (AP) reported on Monday. The report cited State Department documents obtained by AP and two US officials. The visa revocations would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, said the AP report, citing officials.

items.title: Social media and FOMO fuel investment scams [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Investment scam syndicates are increasingly exploiting social media, online relationships and victims' "fear of missing out" to lure Malaysians into fraudulent schemes. Instead, syndicates use multiple digital platforms to identify potential victims and draw them into fraudulent investments. Rusdi said syndicates promoted purported investments ranging from Ponzi schemes to cryptocurrency and gold.

items.title: Two retirees lose RM750,000 after falling for investment scams
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: She lost more than RM500,000 of her retirement savings to an investment scam. The 69-year-old woman urges others, particularly those investing their savings, not to be swayed by promises of attractive returns. She was introduced by an agent to several investment schemes promising lucrative returns.

items.title: Buying strata? New housing policy proposes showing long-term maintenance costs upfront, tighter management rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Buying a strata property could eventually involve more than knowing the purchase price, monthly instalment and maintenance fee. With the recently launched National Housing Policy or Dasar Perumahan Negara (DRN) 2026-2035, the government proposes factoring longer-term maintenance and replacement costs into sale and purchase agreements for strata housing. It is among several measures in the DRN aimed at improving the long-term maintenance and management of housing, including better maintenance planning, professional building management and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757).

items.title: Terengganu Perhilitan moves rescued elephant to Perak
items.summary: TERENGGANU Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has relocated a female elephant that was found roaming around Kampung Jeram, Manir, last Friday. Its director, Dennis Ten, said the elephant was rescued on Saturday. The relocation began at 8am yesterday and involved 13 members from Terengganu Perhilitan, seven from Sungai Deka Elephant Conservation Centre and two from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Kuala Gandah, Pahang.

items.title: Trump threatens to rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was considering renaming Lake Ontario as "Lake America" as his trade war with Canada escalated. "The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don't expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer," Trump said on his Truth Social network. Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes located on the border between Canada and the United States.

items.title: Penang schools to halt outdoor activities if API reading tops 100
items.summary: PENANG schools have been ordered to halt outdoor activities if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100 as part of the state's haze preparedness measures. The state Education Department said schools must also close immediately once the API reading exceeded 200, in line with existing guidelines. The department said schools and district education offices had been directed to monitor official readings from the Department of Environment.

items.title: Miti to implement low-altitude economy project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry will implement the Unmanned Valley Ecosystem pilot project to drive the development of the low-altitude economy (LAE). LAE refers to economic activities and public services conducted within a low-altitude airspace ecosystem using technologies such as drones, advanced air mobility, air logistics, infrastructure inspection, smart farming and emergency services. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the project would be carried out under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), with the proposed pilot project to be located at universities.

items.title: TH RCI: MCW questions why former auditor general not called to testify
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Corruption Watch (MCW) has questioned whether all evidence relating to the Tabung Haji (TH) issue was fairly tested before conclusions were reached by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), particularly given that former Auditor-General Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad was not called to testify. MCW said the RCI report showed that Madinah had submitted a statutory declaration as a witness but was not called to give evidence before the commission. Madinah said the 2017 Auditor-General's Report, prepared by her and her team, did not identify evidence of direct theft at TH.

items.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on US$20 billion worth of US goods
items.summary: OTTAWA: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion (US$19.94 billion) worth of United States goods, matching dollar-for-dollar new duties imposed by Washington, and unveiled financial support for Canadian businesses and workers caught in the escalating trade war. From Saturday, President Donald Trump's new 50 per cent tariffs across US$20 billion of Canadian imports took effect after talks between the two countries to avert the tariffs collapsed. The new tit-for-tat tariffs mark a new low in the Canada-US relationship.

items.title: Ramkarpal urges govt to expedite Sosma amendments
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Gelugor member of parliament Ramkarpal Singh has urged the government to announce when amendments to Sosma will be tabled, saying the delay requires urgent attention. Ramkarpal, who is DAP national legal bureau chairman, said he took note of former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay's defence of the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma). Ayob had said specialised laws were necessary to deal effectively with terrorism and organised crime.

items.title: Don't repeat RCI just because findings don't suit, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was established to seek the truth based on facts and evidence, not to yield decisions in favour of any political party, says PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. "When the RCI findings do not favour their political narrative, suddenly they want a new RCI. "Should a new RCI be established every time an investigation's findings do not meet their political expectations, until a decision they like is reached?"

items.title: Celebrity preacher, NGO secretary to face RM12.3mil misappropriation charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will charge the chairman of a non-governmental organisation (NGO), who is also a celebrity preacher, and the NGO's secretary at the Seremban Sessions Court tomorrow over the alleged misappropriation of more than RM12 million. On April 22, the Negri Sembilan MACC was reported to have arrested a freelance preacher suspected of abusing his position and misappropriating about RM12.3 million in NGO funds for personal gain. Following the investigation, the Negri Sembilan MACC froze 15 accounts comprising three personal accounts, three NGO accounts and nine company accounts, with a total value of about RM16.5 million.

items.title: Drafting of new E-Commerce Act must be expedited, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The drafting of a new E-Commerce Act must be expedited to strengthen consumer protection and ensure micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and local traders can compete fairly in an increasingly complex digital ecosystem. She said the country's e-commerce framework must keep pace with technological advancements and changing consumer and business practices. "We need to protect MSMEs and local traders.

items.title: From Tokyo to London, heatwaves send men to work in shorts
items.summary: SCORCHING summer temperatures have done what decades of dress-down Fridays have failed to do — get men to the office in shorts. Major retailers said linen shorts and suits were flying off the shelves in Britain, as men opted for breathable fabrics more commonly associated with Mediterranean climes. Hugo Boss said it has increased its assortment of tailored shorts.

items.title: Azmin rules out PKR return, vows to stay with Bersatu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, who is now with Bersatu, will not return to his former party despite an open invitation to past members. "Bersatu's time will come. Former PKR vice-president Datuk Dr Xavier Jayakumar also confirmed he had rejoined the party.

items.title: Crude volume debate masks real shortage of refined fuels
items.summary: THE crude oil market is currently engaged in the wrong debate over how much oil is actually moving via the Strait of Hormuz. It should be debating the constrained flows of refined products around Asia. Asia's imports of light and middle distillates for this month are estimated by Kpler at 5.59 million bpd, in line with the 5.60 million bpd seen last month.

items.title: NST Leader: Rise and rise of haze hotspots
items.summary: Yet here we are again, with unhealthy air spreading across Peninsular Malaysia and experts warning that the haze could persist until late September. Thanks to prevailing winds from Kalimantan and Sumatra in Indonesia, transboundary haze has reached Sarawak and several locations in the west coast of the peninsula. Indonesia's enforcement record deserves tougher scrutiny.

items.title: Man killed, another arrested after group fight in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police have arrested a man following a group fight at Jalan Mandolin 33/5, Taman Alam Megah, which resulted in the death of another man. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said police were alerted after a member of the public reported a fight involving a group of men. Police subsequently arrested a man in connection with the incident.

items.title: Anwar pays tribute to 'Father of MRSM' Abdul Wahab Alwi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended his condolences to the family of Maktab Rendah Sains Mara (MRSM) founder Abdul Wahab Alwi, who died early this morning. In a Facebook post, Anwar described Abdul Wahab, known as the "Father of MRSM", as having made significant contributions to national education. Abdul Wahab died at 3am today.

items.title: Agriculture, logistics set to reap early gains from Malaysia's low-altitude economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Agriculture and logistics are expected to see the most immediate benefits from the development of Malaysia's low-altitude economy (LAE), according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). The LAE refers to economic activities conducted in lower airspace using drones, unmanned aircraft and air taxis for purposes including agriculture, deliveries, infrastructure inspection, surveillance, mapping, disaster response and passenger transport. CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said drones were already being used in plantations in northern Malaysia for various agricultural activities.

items.title: Teen dies after being struck by lorry following motorcycle fall
items.summary: KOTA BELUD: A 16-year-old student was killed after being hit by a lorry after the motorcycle he was riding skidded on Jalan Kota Belud-Kota Marudu near Kampung Jawi-Jawi here this evening. District police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said preliminary investigations found that the 46-year-old lorry driver was travelling from Kota Marudu towards Tuaran. He said the victim was riding a Yamaha Ego motorcycle with a 15-year-old pillion rider from Sembirai towards Kudat.

items.title: Myanmar man to be charged with sexually assaulting Australian boy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 30-year-old Myanmar national will be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow with sexually assaulting a 3-year-old Australian boy. Northeast district deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake confirmed that the suspect would face a charge under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. The victim's family caught the suspect in the act and immediately lodged a police report, leading to his arrest at the scene.

items.title: Three killed in two-car crash in Kota Tingg
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Three people, including a woman, were killed in a collision involving two cars along Jalan Jemaluang here today. The Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations centre said it received an emergency call about the crash at 5.05pm, prompting the dispatch of teams from the Kota Tinggi and Mersing fire stations. "Upon arrival, firefighters found the crash involved a Honda City carrying a 21-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman, and a Toyota Vios driven by a 31-year-old man.

items.title: Firefighters recover woman's body from 8th floor
items.summary: BAYAN LEPAS: Firefighters were called in to recover the body of a 25-year-old woman from the eighth floor of a building in Batu Maung here today. The Bayan Baru Fire and Rescue Station received a request for assistance from police at 9.19am. According to a post on the Bayan Baru Fire and Rescue Station's Facebook page, firefighters confirmed upon arrival that the woman's body was at the location and began efforts to safely recover it.

items.title: Search ongoing for missing 26-year-old Kafa teacher in Bayan Lepas
items.summary: BALIK PULAU: Police have urged the public not to spread unverified information or speculate about the disappearance of a 26-year-old Kafa teacher. Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said investigations and efforts to locate Mohamad Hijazi Zamri were ongoing. "Police are also scrutinising information circulating about the case," he said today, warning that unverified claims could cause public concern and disrupt the investigation.

items.title: MyKad printing services nationwide to face temporary disruption from tomorrow to Aug 31
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — MyKad printing services nationwide are expected to experience temporary disruption starting tomorrow (Aug 26) until Aug 31 following the transition process to the new generation MyKad. The National Registration Department (JPN) said it was currently implementing the transition from the existing MyKad structure to the new generation identity card. “For first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children, parents or guardians are also encouraged to wait a while to enable their children to receive the new generation MyKad when production begins in the near future,” JPN said in a statement today.

items.title: Public toilets maintained, markets upgraded, drains improved: Housing Ministry says six initiatives surpass targets
items.summary: He said the public toilet maintenance initiative in PBT areas, which received an allocation of RM30 million, recorded the strongest performance at 734 per cent, with 367 projects successfully implemented compared with the original target of 50 projects. Nga said the construction of Madani stalls and upgrading of dilapidated public markets recorded an achievement rate of 170 per cent, with 102 projects implemented compared with the target of 60 projects, involving an allocation of RM60 million. Nga said the initiative to upgrade drainage and sewerage systems recorded an achievement rate of 102.67 per cent, with 154 projects implemented compared with the target of 150 projects, involving an allocation of RM55 million.

items.title: Sunway Lagoon says cooperating with authorities after roller coaster incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Theme Parks says that it is currently working closely and fully cooperating with all relevant authorities as they conduct a thorough investigation into the incident involving an attraction at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday, which affected 10 guests. Confirming the incident, the company also expressed deep regret, saying that their thoughts are with the guests and their families. “Sunway Theme Parks takes this matter extremely seriously.

items.title: Jeffrey Cheah says metal fatigue possible cause of Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has reportedly confirmed a roller coaster accident that injured 10 people occurred at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday. The New Straits Times reported Cheah as saying authorities were investigating the incident, while he believed metal fatigue may have been a possible cause. Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat previously said 22 people, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44, were on the ride when the incident occurred at about 9pm on Saturday.

items.title: Strong winds, heavy rain damage Kuching International Airport roof (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 25 — A section of the roof at the arrival area of Kuching International Airport (KIA) was damaged by strong winds and heavy rain today afternoon. The section of roofing which collapsed due to strong winds on Aug 25, 2026 at Kuching International Airport. The affected areas include Limbang, Miri (Marudi, Telang Usan, Bario and Beluru), Bintulu, Kapit (Kapit, Song and Bukit Mabong), Sarikei (Julau and Pakan), Sibu, Kuching (Kuching), Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman (Lingga, Pantu and Sri Aman), Betong (Pusa) and Mukah (Mukah).

items.title: MetMalaysia: Weak 3.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Batu Pahat
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 25 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.1 magnitude struck the waters off Batu Pahat, Johor, at 4.12pm today. In a statement, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the epicentre was located at coordinates 1.7 degrees north and 102.8 degrees east, about 18 kilometres (km) south-west of Batu Pahat. “There is no tsunami threat to Malaysia,” it said in the statement issued today by the National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre, MetMalaysia.

items.title: National Day 2026: Putrajaya road closures begin tomorrow, only two bridges to remain open
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will step up security and traffic controls in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya from tomorrow ahead of the 69th Merdeka Eve celebrations and National Day 2026. He said eight major roads would be closed from 6am to noon for rehearsals on Aug 28 and 29: Dataran Putra, Persiaran Perdana, Laman Perdana, Jalan P2a, Jalan P2t, Jalan P2s, Jalan P2w, and Jalan P2y. “The affected routes include Seri Wawasan Bridge, Seri Saujana Bridge, Seri Gemilang Bridge, Putra Bridge and Seri Ehsan Bridge, while only Seri Bestari Bridge and Seri Setia Bridge will remain open to traffic,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Yayasan Tunku Abdul Rahman marks 60 years with RM96.6m poured into youth empowerment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Yayasan Tunku Abdul Rahman (YTAR) is celebrating six decades of empowering young Malaysian talent, having channelled RM96.6 million in scholarships, financial aid, and leadership development to more than 12,000 youths since its inception in 1966. The foundation marked its diamond jubilee at a commemorative event in Kuala Lumpur on August 13, where National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang highlighted the foundation’s enduring contribution to national development. Since its founding, YTAR has focused on equipping high-potential, underserved youths with the resources, leadership skills, and ethical grounding required to shape Malaysia’s future.

items.title: PAS muktamar to debate Umno ties and Muslim unity, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — A motion addressing political cooperation between Umno and PAS will be tabled at the Islamist party’s upcoming annual muktamar, PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today. Speaking after attending the forum “Reality and Perception: Don’t Politicise Tabung Haji”, Takiyuddin said that bridging ties across the Malay-Muslim political landscape is a central pillar for the party assembly, FMT reported. “One of the motions that will certainly be discussed is Muslim unity, as well as political cooperation between PAS and Umno.

items.title: Prisoner dies in Marang after alleged beating by three inmates over old debt
items.summary: MARANG, Aug 25 — A male prisoner died after he was believed to have been beaten by three other inmates at a prison in the district yesterday. Marang District Police chief Supt Sofian Redzuan said police received a report of the case at 12.31pm yesterday, and the incident was believed to have stemmed from an old debt and the three suspects’ dissatisfaction with the victim. “The victim, who was from Terengganu, was beaten in a room by three suspects aged between 21 and 35.

items.title: High Court slashes man’s rape sentence from 10 years to one, citing youth and rehabilitation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The High Court in Kuantan has slashed a man’s sentence for statutory rape from 10 years’ imprisonment and six strokes of the cane to one year’s jail and two strokes. In allowing the 23-year-old’s appeal against the penalty, Judicial Commissioner Samry Masri ruled that the Sessions Court had failed to give adequate weight to the accused’s youth, his clean record as a first offender, and his strong prospects for rehabilitation, FMT reported. The Sessions Court had handed down five years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the rotan for each charge, ordering the sentences to run consecutively.

items.title: Police: Plantation supervisor seriously injured in machete attack at workers’ quarters in Gua Musang
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 25 — A plantation supervisor was seriously injured after being attacked by a group of individuals armed with machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs during an altercation at a workers’ quarters in Kampung RKT Kesedar Chalil, Gua Musang, yesterday. Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said the incident occurred at about 3.15pm after a group of men, believed to be representatives of a company with interests in the area, arrived at the quarters to seek clarification regarding permits to enter a forest reserve. A plantation worker who attempted to intervene was subsequently attacked by the group using weapons such as machetes, iron rods and wooden clubs,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Zahid backs PAC move to probe Tabung Haji management since 2017, stresses facts over perception
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi supports a proposal for the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to establish a special body to investigate the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2017 to the present. Ahmad Zahid said the investigation was important to clarify what had happened after 2017 based on facts and reality, while also helping to correct public perceptions regarding TH’s management and governance. Asked whether the proposal to establish the special body would be brought to the Cabinet, Ahmad Zahid said this was unnecessary as the PAC has the appropriate mandate and responsibility to conduct the investigation.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART rescue team prepares for United Nations reclassification, aims to retain status
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (SMART) is determined to retain its Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (Heavy USAR) classification under the United Nations (UN) as a special “gift” to Malaysia in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations. SMART Team Commander PgKB I Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the country’s elite rescue team is scheduled to undergo the INSARAG External Reclassification (IER) assessment from Sept 20 to 24 to retain the classification, which it first obtained in 2016. Abdul Manaf expressed confidence in SMART’s level of preparedness after undergoing three large-scale pre-IER exercises, including one simulation last year and two this year.

items.title: Lee Lam Thye urges urgent review of Asean haze pact, calls for enforceable action plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Asean leaders have been urged to conduct an urgent high-level review of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution and adopt a stronger, time-bound and enforceable regional action plan to prevent the haze situation from worsening. Social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said the recurring transboundary haze crisis could no longer be treated as a seasonal inconvenience, saying that Asean must move from reaction to prevention and strengthen regional preparedness. “We must stop treating haze as an annual Asean ritual.

items.title: Man arrested in Chow Kit hotel over Quran burning, theft investigations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 25 — Police arrested a man at a hotel in Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur, yesterday to assist investigations into the burning and theft of copies of the Quran. Negeri Sembilan Police Chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the 25-year-old suspect was arrested following a public complaint about a fire near a field in Senawang on Aug 22. “Investigations revealed that the fire involved several copies of the Quran.

items.title: Hot weather and strong winds complicate firefighting as 51‑hectare Kota Tinggi peat blaze rages
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Aug 25 — Hot weather and strong winds are complicating efforts to put out a 51.4-hectare peat fire along Jalan Bypass Sebana Cove-Punggai that started yesterday. Operations commander, Deputy Fire Supt II Baharuddin Idris said 9.7 per cent of the fire in Sector A, which is 35.6 hectares, and the entire area of Sektor B (15.8 hectares), was under control “Our main challenges are strong winds, hot weather and limited water supply. Fire and Rescue Department personnel battling the blaze along the Punggai–Sebana Cove bypass.

items.title: Thousands join Maulidur Rasul nationwide, Anwar leads UPM procession under Madani Dihayati theme
items.summary: At the national level, the celebration at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), Serdang was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, with more than 4,000 people, including procession contingents. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee. Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin, Selangor Islamic Religious Council chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin and State Islamic Religion and Cultural Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohamad Fahmi Ngah.

items.title: Malaysians advised to reconsider non‑essential travel to Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat amid unrest
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 25 — Malaysians in Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, as well as those planning to travel there, have been urged to remain vigilant following a series of recent security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces. Malaysia’s Consul General in Songkhla, Thailand, Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi, said those planning to travel to the affected areas were advised to reconsider non-essential travel. “Malaysians are also advised to avoid areas affected by security incidents, demonstrations or large gatherings and to comply with instructions from the Thai authorities, including those on curfews, road closures and security checks,” he said in a statement from Istana Arau today.

items.title: Prime Minister urges Muslims to reflect Prophet’s values, not limit Maulidur Rasul to celebrations
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the commemoration of Maulidur Rasul should not be limited to celebrations or processions, but should instead be reflected through practising Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) way of life as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. He said the Maulidur Rasul celebration should serve as a platform to inspire Muslims with renewed spirit, awareness and enlightenment. Every episode in the life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) offers a lesson for us,” he said in his speech at the national-level Maulidur Rasul 1448/2026 celebration here today.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore reaffirm commitment to free and safe Strait of Malacca
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Aug 25 — Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore reaffirmed their shared commitment to keep the Strait of Malacca and Singapore Strait free, open and safe for international shipping. The commitment was made by the Malaysia Marine Department, Indonesia’s Directorate General of Sea Transportation, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in a joint statement issued during 17th Co-operation Forum on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) are a primary artery for global trade, with more than 100,000 vessels passing through the waterways each year.

items.title: Anwar: Amirudin tasked to work out Pakatan-BN alliance details for Melaka polls
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has been given the mandate to work out the details of proposed cooperation between the coalition and Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election, said PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the prime minister, said Amirudin had been entrusted with looking into the matter. he said.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin calls for less political rivalry among Malaysia’s Muslim leaders
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 25 — The unity of Muslims is facing growing challenges due to differences in politics, religious schools of thought, race and personal interests, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah said. “These include Islamic economics, Islamic finance, the halal industry, waqf, digital dakwah and strengthening family institutions. Also present were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Perak Raja Muda Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.

items.title: Prime Minister confirms Felda forensic audit proposal will be tabled at Cabinet meeting soon
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 25 — A proposal for a forensic audit to be conducted into the management of the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda) will be discussed by the Cabinet, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar was responding to a question about Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s suggestion that a forensic audit be conducted to determine whether there had been abuse of power, breach of trust or governance violations in Felda’s management. Previously, Anwar said he would await the full report by the special task force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.

items.title: Immigration lodges police report after viral UTC Pudu post found inconsistent with CCTV records
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has lodged a police report over a viral post concerning an applicant’s experience at the UTC Pudu Sentral Immigration Branch Office. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said a review found that several allegations in the post were inconsistent with closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, related records and statements from officers on duty at the time of the incident. A police report has been lodged and JIM will provide its full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM),” he said.

items.title: Haze alert: Penang health exco advises face masks as API levels spike
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 25 — Residents of Penang are urged to limit outdoor activities as air quality deteriorated today, with three of the state's four monitoring stations breaching the unhealthy threshold. State youth, sports and health committee chairman Daniel Gooi advised the public to wear face masks when outdoors to mitigate the effects of the poor air quality. According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), readings as of 11am showed unhealthy levels across most of the state.

items.title: MACC probes RM80m Felda Palong 7 oil palm replanting scheme after settlers raise concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is examining information related to the implementation of the oil palm development and replanting programme at Felda Palong 7 in Wilayah Raja Alias, Bandar Sri Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, including concerns over the quality of the seedlings supplied and their compliance with the required specifications. In a statement, MACC said the information was received from Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) chairman Mohd Syahrizal Md Yusuf, who raised concerns over the quality of the oil palm seedlings and the implementation of the programme. The commission said the matters raised included the supply, delivery, storage and age of the oil palm seedlings, as well as whether they complied with the required specifications.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across four states and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Four states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak are expected to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 1 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Selangor, the areas forecast to be hit are Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor and Gombak, while in Sarawak, the areas involved are Bintulu and several areas in Miri, namely Subis, Miri, Beluru and Marudi. Meanwhile, in a separate statement, MetMalaysia also issued a Tropical Storm Advisory (NARRA) after a tropical storm was detected in northwestern China today, but stressed that the phenomenon would not have a significant impact on Malaysia.

items.title: Sarawak and Klang Valley worst hit as 30 spots in Malaysia breach ‘Unhealthy’ API levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Malaysia’s prolonged haze crisis showed no signs of abating today, with 30 monitoring stations nationwide recording “unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels, according to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). Sarawak remained the epicentre of the country's worst air pollution. The IPD Serian monitoring station recorded the highest reading nationwide at 180, inching toward the “very unhealthy” threshold of 201.
